basicLevel.definition: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer
keyPoints: Electrons transfer from metal to non-metal
basicLevel.example: NaCl: Na gives electron to Cl, forming Na+ and Cl−

intermediateLevel.definition: Strong electrostatic force holding together cations and anions in a crystal lattice
keyPoints: Electron transfer from lower electronegativity to higher
Each ion surrounded by ions of opposite charge
intermediateLevel.example: MgO: Mg(2+) and O(2−) in 1:1 ratio with rock salt structure

advancedLevel.definition: Coulombic force (F = kQ₁Q₂/r²) creating ordered arrays with coordination geometry
keyPoints: Coordination number depends on ionic radius ratio
Affects melting point, solubility, and conductivity
advancedLevel.example: NaCl has 6:6 coordination; CsCl has 8:8 coordination due to ion size
